calibration_rulings.title: The order of an area line whose source names no larger place as a bare name ('Al-Battaliyah village — northeast of Hofuf', 'Al-Koot district — central Hofuf').
calibration_rulings.binds: jalaniyah::area, unchanged. BINDS b4: hubaish «محلہ جنوبی الرفعہ، ہفوف کے وسط میں», umzurainiq «محلہ العویمریہ، ہفوف کے وسط میں» and uqair-mosque's area line keep the source's order as they stand. Round 1's six lines (al-uqair, jawatha-mosque, ameeriah, khuzam, baiah, uqair-castle) stand unchanged. Every later area line of the pattern. ROUND 2: unchanged for both batches.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. Where the source's area line names no larger place as a bare name — it gives a village, a quarter or a port and then where that lies by a direction or a part of the town — the Urdu keeps the source's order: the place with its generic, then «،», then the position, which ends in a postposition: «البطالیہ گاؤں، ہفوف کے شمال مشرق میں», «محلہ الکوت، ہفوف کے وسط میں». Ruling P20 is untouched and holds wherever the source names a larger place as a bare name: that place leads («ہفوف، محلہ الکوت»; «الاحساء، مشرقی دیہات میں التہیمیہ گاؤں»). The two orders are therefore two cases of one rule — what the source gives as a bare larger name leads, and what it gives as a position follows — and no line of round 1 moves. Cost, stated: the same quarter can still stand quarter-first on one page and town-first on another where its sources word the line differently; that is logged with the sources' defects and is the owner's to even out in the source. On record for him, one line: B for every such line («ہفوف کے شمال مشرق میں، البطالیہ گاؤں»), which would move ten lines on applied pages.
calibration_rulings.guard: Stage checker: its note of ruling P20 on an area line of this pattern is expected and is not a finding. For the proofreader, not machine-read: an area line that does not open with a bare larger place has a source that names none, and ends in a postposition, never in a bare place name after the comma.

calibration_rulings.title: A Hijri year or century whose Gregorian equivalent the source marks as approximate ('1280 AH (around 1863 CE)', 'the fifth century AH (around the eleventh century CE)').
calibration_rulings.binds: jalaniyah::body (the century), bubakr-ribat::body (two years). BINDS b4, unchanged: hubaish body «تیرہویں صدی ہجری (تقریباً انیسویں صدی عیسوی)». Every later page with such a pair. ROUND 2: unchanged for both batches.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. Where the source gives a Hijri year or century and marks its Gregorian equivalent as approximate, the form is ruling N12's (or N11's) with the one word «تقریباً» inside the round bracket, before the Gregorian figure or ordinal: «1280 ہجری (تقریباً 1863 عیسوی)», «1430 ہجری (تقریباً 2009 عیسوی)», «پانچویں صدی ہجری (تقریباً گیارہویں صدی عیسوی)». The word stands only where the source has it and only on the side the source puts it: where the source's 'around' covers the Hijri date itself it stands before the pair, as on jabri-mosque («تقریباً 850 ہجری (1446 عیسوی)»). Nothing is converted, computed or evened out between pages: 1430 AH is «(2009 عیسوی)» on jalaniyah and «(تقریباً 2009 عیسوی)» on bubakr-ribat because their sources say so.
calibration_rulings.guard: The machine-read clauses of rulings N11 and N12 hold as they are (the stage checker passes this form under both). For the proofreader, not machine-read: the word for 'around' stands inside the bracket only where the source marks the Gregorian side as approximate, and is the round's one word for it.

calibration_rulings.title: Does the name «رباط آل ابی بکر الملا» owe a gloss on its own page (ruling P3c, point 1)?
calibration_rulings.binds: bubakr-ribat: title, summary, body. Any later page whose name begins with «رباط»: bare, with what the place is said in the summary and at the opening of the body.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. No bracket. «رباط» is an Urdu word and not an opaque generic (case a), and it is not shown to be a false friend (case b): the one reader who met it understood what the place is from the page's own words before the body began. The name stands bare in title and body; the summary, which renders first, says what the place is in the source's own words («ایک علمی وقف»), and the second sentence of the body says it again. B's bracket would say «سرائے» of a place the sources call an endowment for students, and C adds a noun neither source has. The word is masculine and the page's own text agrees with it so.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: on bubakr-ribat no bracket follows the name, and the summary and the second sentence of the body say what the place is.

calibration_rulings.title: A «بیت X» name met in passing: bare, or with «نامی» and an Urdu generic (ruling P3c, point 2, lists neither)?
calibration_rulings.binds: dibs::body. Every later passing mention of «بیت البیعہ» or «بیت الملا».
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. «بیت» joins the generics of ruling P3c, point 2, that are Urdu words: a «بیت X» name met in passing stands bare, with no bracket and no «نامی». What the place is belongs to its own page, where its gloss stands by cases (c) and (d). B would call a building «گھر» that is a museum today, which the passing page's source does not say.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: a name that begins with «بیت» and is not the page's title stands bare.

calibration_rulings.title: The gloss of the page's own name on qubba-mosque: an application of ruling P3c, point 1, cases (c) and (d).
calibration_rulings.binds: qubba-mosque::body; the summary and the title carry no bracket.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A, as ruling P3c gives it: «مسجد القبہ (یعنی گنبد والی مسجد)» once, at the first mention in the body, a noun with its describing phrase and no possessive; never in the title, the summary or a label. The summary says the same thing in plain words without the name, as its source does.
calibration_rulings.guard: The machine-read clause of ruling P3c as it is (the opener of the gloss once on a page, straight after the page's own title).

calibration_rulings.title: A byname the source itself quotes and the English translates ('the village of forty mosques'): marks, gloss, «نامی»?
calibration_rulings.binds: tahimiyah-s::body. BINDS b4, as SHARED-05 has it: tahimiyah-e body carries the same clause word for word after its own opening words («خود یہ گاؤں»); its summary, whose English has a count and no byname, keeps «چالیس مساجد» without marks. ROUND 2: unchanged for both batches.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A, as a fourth place for quotation marks beside the three of ruling N16, point 5: a byname that the source itself sets in quotation marks and the English translates is written translated, inside U+201C and U+201D, with no gloss and no «نامی» (it is not a P3b name: nothing of it is Arabic). Its plural is the page's own («مساجد»). The shared clause, from its first word to its stop: «کبھی “چالیس مساجد کا گاؤں” کے نام سے مشہور تھا، اور ان مساجد میں سے اب تقریباً گیارہ ہی باقی ہیں۔» — 'only' is the particle and 'around' the round's one word, both the source's; that the two pull against each other (observation 47) is the source's sentence.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the byname stands inside its quotation marks at every mention, translated, with no bracket after it.

calibration_rulings.title: An Hours value that gives no clock time ('Open to visitors during daylight hours', Arabic 'available for visiting throughout the daylight hours').
calibration_rulings.binds: tahimiyah-s::practical[1].value. BINDS b4, as SHARED-04 has it: tahimiyah-e practical[1].value is this string byte for byte. The label is the approved «اوقات». ROUND 2: unchanged for both batches.
calibration_rulings.ruling: B, one string on both pages: «دن بھر زائرین کے لیے کھلی رہتی ہے». Where the two sources differ in strength the Arabic is followed ('throughout the daylight hours'), and that is counted under accuracy against the English's 'during'. No clock time is supplied, nothing is tied to prayer times, and the row is carried into no other field. That an Hours row stands on a mosque page beside the owner's fixed row, and what the owner's pending question would make of it, is logged for him; neither wording answers it.
calibration_rulings.guard: The two values are equal by script. For the proofreader, not machine-read: the value names no hour and ends without a stop.

calibration_rulings.title: A mosque with more than one prayer niche and with arches named in the same breath: ruling N34 marks the niche by the singular, which cannot hold here.
calibration_rulings.binds: jalaniyah::body. b4: its pages with arches (hubaish, umzurainiq) name no niche in the plural beside them and are not touched; the rule binds b4 only if such a sentence arises.
calibration_rulings.ruling: E. Round 1 ruled B and named the next blind reader as its test; B failed it and is withdrawn. On a page where niches in the plural and arches both stand, they do not share a sentence, and the arches are said first, among the materials and the roof and before any niche has been named: «ستونوں کی قطاروں پر نوک دار محرابیں ٹکی ہیں۔» Then the niches, with the wall and their number: «قبلے کی دیوار میں دو محرابیں اس مسجد کو منفرد بناتی ہیں۔» No word changes and none is added; the order of two statements of one source sentence is turned, which is form (ruling P23). D is not taken: ruling N34 keeps one word for the arch and a batch judge does not reopen it. C drops the source's noun. The cost of E is on record: one word still names two things in neighbouring sentences, and E has been read by no one; the next blind reader is its test. IF HE STUMBLES TOO, nothing inside ruling N34 is left to try: the text is then locked with E or B, whichever that round's judge finds the less harmful, and the cure both readers of this batch wrote, D, goes to whoever may reopen N34 — its mark for the arch (the plural) fails on a page whose niches are plural. ‖ AFTER THE LAST BLIND READ (b3/stages/06-blind-reader.on-r2.md, item 12, moderate; no judge round followed it): the reader of E stumbled too. He took the second sentence for two of the arches, read it twice, and wrote the word of candidate D for the first sentence. The final text carries E; D goes to whoever may reopen ruling N34.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: on jalaniyah the sentence of the arches stands before the sentence of the two niches, and the two are two sentences.

calibration_rulings.title: The Urdu title where title_en keeps only the place name and translates the rest ('Al-Tahimiyah West Mosque').
calibration_rulings.binds: tahimiyah-s::title. BINDS b4, as SHARED-02 has it: tahimiyah-e «التہیمیہ کی مشرقی مسجد»; uqair-mosque's title is built the same way. ROUND 2: unchanged for both batches.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A, one pattern for a title whose English translates everything but the place name: the place name as its key, the Urdu possessive, then the translated words in Urdu order — «التہیمیہ کی مغربی مسجد», «التہیمیہ کی مشرقی مسجد». The note ruling N14 added to the title rule (the Arabic generic first) is for names whose generic the English keeps, and is not touched.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: such a title begins with the place name as its termbase key writes it, and carries no Arabic adjective with an article.

calibration_rulings.title: The Royal Commission for Jubail and Yanbu: the Urdu adjective for 'royal', or the press's loan?
calibration_rulings.binds: jalaniyah::body. BINDS b4, as SHARED-08 has it: uqair-mosque body writes the same key in the same oblique form. ROUND 2: unchanged for both batches.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. The body is «الجبیل اور ینبع کا شاہی کمیشن»: the Urdu adjective for 'royal', the loan ruling N18 admits for a body called a commission, the two cities with the Urdu possessive; no quotation marks, and it inflects like any phrase (ruling N16, point 4) — in a sentence «الجبیل اور ینبع کے شاہی کمیشن نے». The press form goes to the entry for search and is not written. The entry stays pending for one reason only: nothing in Urdu attests this wording for this body.
calibration_rulings.guard: Proofreader, checklist item 9: «کمیشن» stands here in the name of a body (ruling N18). Not machine-read: the name carries no quotation marks.

calibration_rulings.title: A named quarter inside a district that already carries the round's district word (Arabic «محلة الرويضة بحي الكوت»).
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. A quarter inside a district is named after the district with «نامی حصے»: «محلہ الکوت کے الرویضہ نامی حصے میں»; the district word is written once. In the area line the town leads as a bare name (ruling P20) and the line ends in the postposition: «ہفوف، محلہ الکوت کے الرویضہ نامی حصے میں».
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the district word stands once in such a phrase.

calibration_rulings.title: The sentence 'in 2017 it was listed among Al-Ahsa's officially registered historic mosques' (jalaniyah here, tahimiyah-e in b4): SHARED-12 of stage 4, changed by round 1 of b3's stage 7.
calibration_rulings.binds: jalaniyah::body. BINDS b4: tahimiyah-e body changes its sentence to exactly «2017 میں یہ الاحساء کی تاریخی مساجد کی سرکاری فہرست میں شامل ہوئی۔» — the same string in both batches from its first figure to its stop. Every later page that names the register. ROUND 2: unchanged — the same exact string for both batches; b4's text carries it since b4's round 1 (tahimiyah-e body).
calibration_rulings.ruling: B. One Urdu name for the one register on every page: «الاحساء کی تاریخی مساجد کی سرکاری فہرست». The sentence with a year is «2017 میں یہ الاحساء کی تاریخی مساجد کی سرکاری فہرست میں شامل ہوئی۔»; the sentence without one stays «… الاحساء کی تاریخی مساجد کی سرکاری فہرست میں درج ہیں» (tahimiyah-s). The year stays bare (ruling N12). It is a change of form under ruling P23 — the year, the list, its being official and the mosques being historic all stand — and it is counted under accuracy; A stays on record as the literal wording for the owner. SHARED-12 as stage 4 worded it is withdrawn.
calibration_rulings.guard: Stage checker: the string «جو سرکاری طور پر درج ہیں» does not occur. For the proofreader, not machine-read: the two sentences of jalaniyah and tahimiyah-e are equal by script.

calibration_rulings.title: 'The oasis' on a page whose text nowhere names the oasis ('the depth of learning in the oasis', 'an entire era of the oasis's history').
calibration_rulings.binds: bubakr-ribat::body, qubba-mosque::body: both leaves were changed in b3's round 2 (its changes 2, 3 and 5), and the sentence of the oasis in each is unchanged. b4: no string of its present text has the word for an oasis; the ruling binds b4, and every later page, only where a page mentions the oasis and no field of it names it. The calibration page and the pages of round 1: not bound as text, and not failed.
calibration_rulings.ruling: C, with the scope the evidence supports. A page that mentions the oasis names it at least once in its own text, in the form rulings P8 and N16 give: «الاحساء کے نخلستان», in the direct case «الاحساء کا نخلستان». Where a source says 'the oasis' on a page no field of which names it, the Urdu names it at that mention: so on bubakr-ribat and qubba-mosque. On a page that does name the oasis, the bare noun and the noun with a demonstrative may stand elsewhere. The ruling is NOT a rule about the first mention and NOT a rule about a summary read on its own: the calibration page (bare noun in the summary, the name at the opening of the body) is neither changed nor failed by it, and no page of round 1 is. B is not taken: it drops the source's noun. No fact enters: the oasis the source means is named, as its article names it. Cost, stated: on qubba-mosque the name lengthens a chain of possessives to four (charged under nativeness on that page).
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: a page of round 2 or later whose text has the word for an oasis has «الاحساء کے نخلستان» or «الاحساء کا نخلستان» in at least one of its fields. This is no test of which mention comes first and no test of a summary taken alone; a check written from it passes the calibration page as it stands.

calibration_rulings.title: The common noun for a governor before a name (Arabic «الوالي العثماني محمد فروخ باشا»).
calibration_rulings.binds: dibs::body. b4: its present text names no governor; the word binds it, and every later page, where one is named.
calibration_rulings.ruling: C. Before a name, a governor is «حاکم». The word of A is not written as a common noun before a name on these pages, because unvocalised it is the everyday feminine suffix and was read so. B is refused under the owner's rule as it stands (P16): a common Urdu word exists, and a reader's preference does not open the door to a loan. Cost, stated: «حاکم» is a shade wider than the Arabic's title (it is also said of a ruler); the adjective before it and the title «پاشا» after the name keep the sense.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: on dibs the word before the governor's name is «حاکم», and the only other «والی» of the page is the suffix in «ساتھ والی سڑک».

open_items.provisional: لم يُختبر: لا ضمير من هذه الفئة ولا «ڑھ» في الصفحة. المؤقت: «ہ» (U+06C1) في الضمائر كما يحصر ملف الدور 05 استعمال U+06BE في المهموسات المعدودة؛ و«ڑھ» مهموس حقيقي، فعلى الفواحص قبول U+06BE بعد U+0691. ‖ b0-ui round 3: Stays open. The other half of the item, the aspirate after U+0691, is ruled below (P22a). ‖ b2 round 3: Stays open for the pronouns. P22a adopted.

open_items.provisional: Not ruled by the translation line: a brand name is not coined or transliterated here (N1). The key stays undefined and the Latin wordmark renders, as in the three earlier lines.
open_items.first_bites: every /ur/ page that is listed: its tab title, og:site_name and the footer; the owner's to decide

open_items.title: A quoted Arabic word that is letter for letter an Urdu word («حسی», the singular of the name, reads as the adjective 'sensory'): how is the reader told what he is looking at?
open_items.provisional: Not settled: stays open. C is withdrawn — tried, read, no cure, and a word neither source carries; the conditions under which round 2 let it in (P23: the repaired text passes a blind read) were not met. The text stands in the wording of round 1, «لفظ “الاحساء”، “حسی” کی جمع ہے، یعنی …»: the order the first reader asked for and the second read without remark on the order. The homograph remains and is charged under fit. B, the remedy three readers ask for and the form the Arabic source itself uses, is barred by the P8 build guard (U+0650) and by ruling P17 as they stand, and a judge does not reopen a ruling. Recorded for whoever may: the build guard already exempts a termbase key that carries the sign (tools/check-ur-text.mjs, the registered-key exemption of P8), so the vocalised word would need an entry whose key carries the kasra and the sukun, the stage checker to honour the same exemption for a key the chain proposes, and the two signs in the Nastaliq subset.
open_items.first_bites: the home page as it stands; any later sentence that quotes an Arabic word which unvocalised spells an Urdu word (the etymology of a name, a dish, a craft term)
